name: cloud-init-debian
stdout:
#cloud-config
#
# preview-host for *.preview.example.com  —  CONTROL STACK ONLY, no shared services.
#
#   hcloud server create --name preview-host --type cx32 --image debian-12 \
#     --ssh-key <your-key> --user-data-from-file user-data.yaml
#
#   hcloud server ssh preview-host -- cloud-init status --wait
#   hcloud server ssh preview-host -- tail -40 /var/log/cloud-init-output.log
#
# ── GENERATED ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Rendered by `pstack cloud-init` for preview.example.com. Every value below is already filled in; read
# it before booting a host with it, but there are no placeholders left to substitute.
#
# ── DNS, BEFORE YOU BOOT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Two A records at your DNS provider, both pointing at the server's IPv4:
#
#     preview.example.com.       A   <server-ip>
#     *.preview.example.com.     A   <server-ip>
#
# The wildcard is what makes per-PR hostnames free — `backend-pr-7.preview.example.com` resolves
# with no per-PR DNS work. Note it matches ONE label: `backend-pr-7.preview.example.com` is
# covered, `backend.pr-7.preview.example.com` is NOT. Flatten per-PR hostnames with dashes.
#
# ── TLS: HTTP-01, so there is no DNS credential anywhere in this file ────────────────────────
# Traefik answers the challenge on port 80, so **port 80 must be reachable from the internet** —
# do not firewall it off "because everything is HTTPS". The web→websecure redirect does not break
# it: Traefik installs an internal ACME router at maximum priority that bypasses the redirect for
# /.well-known/acme-challenge/.
#
# The cost of HTTP-01: it CANNOT issue wildcards, so every hostname gets its own certificate.
# Let's Encrypt allows ~50 new certificates per registered domain per week, so at ~3 surfaces per
# PR that is roughly **16 new PRs/week** before issuance starts failing — and a preview URL is not
# valid until its container actually exists. When you outgrow that, switch to a wildcard by adding
#     --challenge dns01 --dns-provider <lego-code>
# plus PSTACK_DNS_TOKEN=… to the `pstack init` call. Nothing else changes.
#
# ── NO SHARED STACK (deliberate, for now) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This host runs the CONTROL stack only: Traefik + pstack (API + UI). There are no `kind: shared`
# deployments yet — no shared database, no shared queue.
#
# `pstack init` still creates the `preview-shared` network, because every per-PR compose file
# declares it `external: true` and would fail to start without it. It will simply be empty.
#
# What that means for your per-PR specs, concretely:
#   - Do NOT add a `requires:` entry asserting a shared service is reachable. There is nothing to
#     assert, and the preflight would fail every deploy.
#   - Anything a preview needs that would normally be shared (a Postgres, a Redis) must either be
#     its own container inside the per-PR compose project, or an off-box service reached over the
#     internet.
#   - When you do add one later: write a `kind: shared` spec, submit it, `up` it once, and only
#     then add the matching `requires:` to your per-PR spec. Order matters — the requirement is
#     checked before anything is created.
#
# ── SECRETS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Nothing in this file is a credential except the dashboard password: HTTP-01 needs no DNS token,
# and PSTACK_TOKEN is generated by `init` and printed once into /var/log/cloud-init-output.log.
# Read it from there, store it in your password manager, then use it as the API bearer token.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The `docker` group must exist before the `users` stage — a user cannot join a group that does
# not exist yet, and Docker is not installed until `runcmd`. Docker's postinst reuses this group.
groups:
  - docker

users:
  - default
  - name: preview
    gecos: preview stack operator
    shell: /bin/bash
    groups: [docker]
    sudo: 'ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL'
    lock_passwd: true
    ssh_authorized_keys:
      - ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIGoldenKeyForTheConformanceSuite0000000 golden@example

package_update: true
packages:
  - ca-certificates
  - curl
  - git
  - jq
  - openssl

# No `write_files:` here any more. The catch-all router a dead or sleeping preview link lands on is
# rendered by `pstack init` itself since 0.26.0 (labels on the pstack container, priority 1 over the
# whole `*.preview.example.com`), so it exists on every host — and it is what wakes a sleeping preview.
#
# SWARM. `init` below runs with the default orchestrator (swarm: this host becomes a one-node manager,
# previews deploy as swarm stacks, workers can join from the Swarm page). For workers to join, open
# 2377/tcp, 7946/tcp+udp and 4789/udp between this host and each worker. Pass
#     --orchestrator compose
# to `pstack init` instead to run previews with plain docker compose on this host only.

runcmd:
  # ── 1. Docker + the compose plugin ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Distro-specific, rendered by the generator. Docker itself is DELIBERATELY not version-pinned:
  # per-distro pin syntax is fragile, and the distro/vendor repo's security updates are exactly
  # what a long-lived host wants. Everything pstack-shaped below IS pinned — the reproducibility
  # risk lives there, not here.
  - install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings
  - curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/debian/gpg -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
  - chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
  - >
    echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc]
    https://download.docker.com/linux/debian $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") stable"
    > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list
  - apt-get update
  - DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io
      docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
  - systemctl enable --now docker
  # `docker compose` (the space form) is what pstack shells out to. On distros whose package ships
  # only a standalone `docker-compose` binary, expose it as the CLI plugin too. No-op elsewhere.
  - bash -c 'docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 || { mkdir -p /usr/local/lib/docker/cli-plugins && ln -sf "$(command -v docker-compose)" /usr/local/lib/docker/cli-plugins/docker-compose; }'
  - docker compose version

  # ── 2. pstack — one static binary from GitHub Releases, PINNED ───────────────────────────
  # The version this file was generated by. Unpinned, a re-provision months later installs
  # whatever is latest — potentially a control plane the rest of this file was never written for.
  # (A mere machine RESTART never re-runs this: cloud-init's runcmd is once per instance. The
  # exposure is re-provisioning from a saved copy of this file.) The installer verifies the
  # checksum and puts the binary at /usr/local/bin/pstack; nothing else is installed.
  - bash -c 'curl -fsSL https://github.com/samishal1998/preview-stacks/releases/download/v<VERSION>/install.sh | PSTACK_VERSION=<VERSION> sh'
  - /usr/local/bin/pstack --version

  # ── 3. The control image ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # `pstack init` requires this image to exist locally and deliberately does NOT pull. `build-image`
  # builds it FROM THE INSTALLED BINARY — the binary is the whole application, so no source
  # checkout and no registry are involved. Tags it `pstack:local`, which is PSTACK_IMAGE's
  # default, which is why the init call below passes no PSTACK_IMAGE. Costs ~1 min.
  - /usr/local/bin/pstack build-image

  # ── 4. Traefik dashboard credentials ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Kept OUT of the watched dynamic directory: the file provider would try to parse an htpasswd
  # file as configuration and log a parse error for the whole directory.
  - mkdir -p /etc/traefik/auth
  - bash -c 'echo "admin:$(openssl passwd -apr1 golden-dashboard-password)" > /etc/traefik/auth/dashboard.htpasswd'
  - chmod 0640 /etc/traefik/auth/dashboard.htpasswd

  # ── 5. Optional: your own preview config, for driving the CLI from the host or a cron sweep ──
  # Not needed for the API path — a submitted spec travels over HTTP as a string.
  - mkdir -p /opt/preview
  - chown -R preview:preview /opt/preview

  # ── 6. Stand up the control stack — FROM THE HOST ─────────────────────────────────────────
  # Deliberately the host's job and never the API's: the API runs inside this stack, so it cannot
  # recreate it without killing the process doing the work, and a bad image would leave the box
  # with no control plane and no remote way in.
  #
  # `init` is idempotent — it renders /var/lib/pstack/control/docker-compose.yml, creates the
  # `preview-ingress` and `preview-shared` networks, writes .env (0600) and dns.env, brings up the
  # `pstack-control` project, and WAITS for the API's healthcheck. Re-running it is the upgrade path.
  #
  # No --challenge  ⇒ HTTP-01: no DNS provider, no token, nothing to rotate.
  # No PSTACK_IMAGE ⇒ `pstack:local`, which step 4 just built.
  # No PSTACK_TOKEN ⇒ generated, stored 0600 in control/.env, and printed once (see the header).
  #
  # ONE CERT RULE, worth internalising now: under HTTP-01 each router resolves its own certificate,
  # so a per-PR router DOES need `tls.certresolver=le`. If you later switch to `--challenge dns01`,
  # that inverts — exactly one always-on router requests the wildcard and every per-PR router must
  # carry `tls=true` alone, or each PR orders a separate certificate and burns the weekly limit.
  - >
    /usr/local/bin/pstack init
    --domain preview.example.com
    --acme-email ops@example.com
    --orchestrator swarm

  # ── 7. Verify before walking away ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Host-local only: there is no published host port (pstack is reached through Traefik), and
  # DNS/TLS may not be ready this early. This is the same probe `init` waits on.
  - docker compose -p pstack-control ps
  - docker inspect -f '{{.State.Health.Status}}' "$(docker compose -p pstack-control ps -q pstack)"

  # NOTE: no systemd unit for `pstack serve`. The API is a CONTAINER in the control stack that
  # `init` just created, with `restart: unless-stopped`, so Docker restarts it on boot. A systemd
  # unit would be a second, competing copy fighting over the same registry directory.

final_message: |
  preview-host is up after $UPTIME seconds.

    UI       https://control.preview.example.com
    API      https://api.preview.example.com/api/health
    Traefik  https://traefik.preview.example.com   (admin / the password you set)

  Upgrade later with `pstack upgrade` over SSH — it reuses this token and domain.

  The API bearer token was generated by `pstack init` and printed above in this log
  (/var/log/cloud-init-output.log). Save it now — it is also in
  /var/lib/pstack/control/.env, mode 0600.

  Certificates are requested on the FIRST HTTPS request per hostname and can take a
  minute. If one never arrives, check that port 80 is reachable and see
  `docker compose -p pstack-control logs traefik | grep -i acme`.

  No shared services exist on this host yet. A per-PR spec must not `requires:` one.
stderr:
Traefik dashboard:  admin / golden-dashboard-password
  Save it now — it is hashed into the file, not recoverable from it.

  This file carries that password and your ACME email, and a provider stores
  user-data where any process on the instance can read it. Do not commit it.

  DNS first:  preview.example.com  and  *.preview.example.com   A -> <server-ip>
  HTTP-01 needs port 80 reachable from the internet.
